summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard under Michael Witzel and also studied under Masato Fujii, later holding a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and a visiting post at Brown (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at RPI and Harvard. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1850), Sanskrit College (1853), King's College London (1862), and served as Librarian at the India Office (~1862–1869).

Flavio A. Geisshuesler specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and the University of Virginia (PhD ~2014–2019 under David F. Germano), and held a postdoctoral research post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem under Dan Martin (2019).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas. She also taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). He held posts at Kansai Medical University (1994–2001), ICPBS (2001), and directed the IIBS (~2004) and IRIAB (2009).

Indologist Florinda De Simini completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin (~2009–2013). She held a postdoctoral fellowship at IIAS (2013), visited Hamburg (~2016), and became Associate Professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2016).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London and under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1987).

Francesco Sferra is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Raffaele Torella. He has held professorships and administrative directorships at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002, ~2020) and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010–2016).
Francis Brinkley, a specialist in Japanology, studied at Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1886).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning an MD at Edinburgh (~1780–1783) under John Hope, he served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services (1794–1815) and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

Buddhist studies scholar Francis Harold Cook completed his doctoral requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970; emeritus attested 1989) and chaired the Numata Center (1999).

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed a Master's in Ancient History and doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier at the University of Calicut (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, and Columbia/Union Theological Seminary, he has taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~2004) and held visiting posts at Rome and San Francisco.
Francis Wilford was an Indologist and historian. He served as a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and was Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1799–1822).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a sinologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at Dartmouth and Harvard (PhD ~1942), with additional study under Paul Pelliot, he served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Fordham and Chicago (doctorate ~1984). He was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) before becoming Parkman Professor of Divinity and Director at Harvard (2005, 2010).
Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Munich (~1868–1871) under Martin Haug (~1869–1871).

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy, biology, and Buddhist studies. After degrees from the University of Chile and Harvard (PhD 1970), he taught at the University of Chile, École Polytechnique, CNRS, and the University of Paris (~1986–2001).

Franciscus Verellen specializes in sinology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).
